action.child: provider-retained monotonic rollback witness / GitHub Events API documented durability sufficiency
action.attempt: Using only current public official GitHub documentation, test whether repository Events API retention/visibility plus PushEvent before/head fields provide a documented provider-retained monotonic witness strong enough to detect coherent force rewind without external storage or privileged administration.
observation: GitHub documents that the Events timeline contains at most 300 events and only events created within the past 30 days; events older than 30 days are excluded even when fewer than 300 events exist.
GitHub documents that Events API is not designed for real-time use and event latency can range from 30 seconds to 6 hours.
GitHub documents PushEvent payload fields including a unique push_id, ref, head (post-push ref SHA), and before (pre-push ref SHA).

The reviewed official Events API and event-type documentation does not state an immutable retention guarantee beyond the bounded timeline, a durable total-order guarantee suitable as an append-only witness, or a guarantee that force-rewind history remains retrievable after the documented retention/count bounds expire.
inference: If a relevant PushEvent is still retrievable, before/head can describe the ref transition and may provide useful recent diagnostic evidence.

Because visibility is explicitly bounded to 30 days and 300 events and the endpoint can lag by hours, that activity stream cannot by itself serve as the required durable monotonic witness across an unbounded coherent rollback horizon without an independent persisted anchor.
The existence of before/head fields is therefore not equivalent to documented append-only durability or permanent rollback detectability.
unverified: The reviewed documentation does not explicitly characterize force-push deletion/rewind coverage for every edge case, so no stronger guarantee is inferred from example payloads.
No claim is made that GitHub internally deletes event data after 30 days; only API visibility guarantees documented for this timeline are used.
action.result: REJECT_FOR_PHASE1_MONOTONIC_WITNESS: official GitHub documentation establishes useful PushEvent transition fields but also explicit bounded timeline visibility and non-real-time latency. No documented durability/order property strong enough for an independent monotonic rollback witness was found. The r273 force=false single-ref transaction-record design remains the current Chat-callable baseline, while the independent monotonic rollback-witness child remains unresolved.
action.tested_scope: Public official GitHub documentation for REST Events endpoints and GitHub PushEvent payload semantics only. No O/downstream/other-worker semantics, repository Events endpoint invocation, webhook receiver/storage, audit-log/admin authority, manual attestation, branch/rules administration, hosted compute/storage, external execution, finite monthly/trial/paid quota, added cost, scheduler mutation, same-run retry, or second semantic leaf.
